topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Sofia Moreno (Redwood AE), Derek Chan (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Singh (NorthLake, Head of ML), Tom Reeves (Security Eng), Marta Lopez (Infra), Evan Clarke (Compliance)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to... to talk through your security questions re: Redwood. quick round of intros?
[00:12] Priya: hi, im priya, head of ML, we're building a research-to-prod pipeline for clinical docs so security is kinda... top line.
[00:20] Tom: tom here, security eng, will mainly focus on KMS, auditability, and retention.
[00:27] Marta: infra lead, wants to understand networking (VPC, peering) and on-prem options.
[00:33] Derek: Derek from Redwood, I'll walk through KMS/HSM options and how our routing works across hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:41] Evan: Evan — compliance, curious about SOC2 evidence and data residency constraints for EU PHI-like data.

[01:02] Sofia: for context, NorthLake is exploring hosted first but they may require private or dedicated for regulated datasets; is that right priya?
[01:12] Priya: yes, initial proof of concept will be on de-id data, then might move to sensitive in prod. timeline's tight — Q2 launch goal.
[01:23] Tom: ok, Q2. our blockers: we need customer-managed key option, and logs that tie requests to SSO user, ideally token-level tracing for audit.
[01:38] Derek: absolutely. we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; hosted has a bring-your-own-key flow via cloud KMS with limited HSM options — I know that's sometimes a sticking point.
[01:52] Priya: when you say limited HSM, can you spell that out? like we need FIPS 140-2 cert or HSM-backed keys for certain datasets.
[02:03] Derek: right, hosted by default uses provider KMS (AWS KMS or GCP KMS) with HSM-backed keys depending on region and account — but if you need full control and FIPS attestation we recommend Private deployment with customer HSM, or Dedicated with KMS proxy to your own key material via external KMS. sometimes that path requires a config change and additional network setup.
[02:25] Tom: and for audit logs — what's the retention? we need 7 years for some workflows and immutable logs for certain requests.
[02:34] Sofia: good question. by default hosted has 90 days of detailed traces in the console, longer aggregated metrics for 13 months. for enterprise we have extended retention add-on and can export raw audit logs to your S3/GCS or SIEM for indefinite retention. immutable/worm retention depends on the storage backend; we can push logs to your account to meet legal retention.
[02:58] Marta: is that export push or pull? we want the logs to live in our VPC.
[03:05] Derek: we can stream audit events via a secure connector into customer-owned storage in their VPC or to a private bucket — it's push over a TLS tunnel, or via VPC peering for Dedicated/Private. sometimes the transcript exporter rounds make the connector name wrong in my head, but it's just a secure forwarder.

[03:35] Priya: ok on SSO — we use Okta and have existing SAML assertions with groups. need group-based RBAC so researchers only see models and prompts they own.
[03:47] Sofia: Redwood supports SAML and OIDC IdPs; group mapping to roles is supported at the org and project level. Derek can show the role matrix in the deep-dive.
[03:58] Derek: yeah mapping is straightforward; caveat: in hosted mode some token-level attributions are abstracted — for strict per-user isolation we recommend Dedicated with SAML assertion pass-through, or Private where you can host the control plane behind your IdP.
[04:14] Tom: that sounds like the biggest tradeoff — friction vs control. any limitations re: single-sign on session length and token revocation? we need immediate revocation in case of incidents.
[04:23] Derek: immediate revocation is supported via SCIM de-provisioning plus token revocation API on Dedicated/Private. hosted can propagate deprovisioning within a minute or two but we have customers who require dedicated for instant cut-off.

[04:43] Evan: SOC2 — are you SOC 2 Type II? can we get the report and controls matrix?
[04:50] Sofia: yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 coverage for certain parts; i'll send the most recent report and a controls breakdown. note sometimes vendor names and dates are slightly off on the doc index, but i'll include the attestation and auditor notes.
[05:07] Priya: we'll need the evidence for our procurement review, plus a timeline for onboarding and any required attestation for private deployment.

[05:21] Derek: on encryption in transit at rest — all tokens and payloads are TLS 1.2+ in transit; at rest defaults to provider-managed encryption, but as discussed you can bring keys for Dedicated/Private. we also support envelope encryption for model cache and KV cache — sometimes people call it "kay-vee cache" and that gets mis-typed in notes.
[05:41] Marta: does envelope encryption affect latency? we have strict latency SLOs for inference.
[05:48] Derek: slight overhead on first token due to decrypt, but we use local cache of DEKs so subsequent tokens minimal impact. we'll run a latency bench for your workload during pilot.

[06:10] Priya: about data residency — we serve from multiple regions, can we pin requests to eu-west-1 for EU patients?
[06:18] Derek: yes routing policies let you pin region and failover; for strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated in the chosen region. hosted can be region-restricted but there are caveats around fallbacks and ephemeral logging in control plane region. we'll document the flow.

[06:36] Tom: any SOC2 gap around third-party sub processors? we need a list.
[06:42] Sofia: we'll share the sub-processor list, and highlight the ones with direct access to data. typical ones are cloud provider, CDN, observability vendor — full list in the security portal.

[07:00] Marta: network connectivity: we want VPC peering + egress control, maybe private link. supported?
[07:07] Derek: yes Dedicated supports VPC peering and PrivateLink; Private deployment can be fully air-gapped or customer network-only. hosted has network options but not full isolation unless you choose Dedicated or Private.

[07:25] Evan: on RBAC — can we do least-privilege for service accounts and route-level API keys? we want token scoping per model and per route.
[07:34] Derek: yes token scoping is supported; service accounts can be scoped to model, route, and rate limit. audit logs record the token id and mapped user — again for hosted we maintain some abstraction but exportable to your SIEM.

[08:00] Priya: about deletion and retention for prompt data — we keep prompts for caching and evals; can we opt out and have immediate deletion on request?
[08:11] Sofia: retention policy is configurable; default is 90 days for host, but we can set near-term deletion for pilot. note: some features like caching reduce cost so you may want limited retention. we'll share retention controls and API for deletion.

[08:35] Tom: legal needs an exportable proof of deletion for e-discovery — do you provide certificates or logs for deletions?
[08:42] Derek: we can provide deletion logs and hashes proving object removal; for Private deployment you control the storage so you can provide your own WORM proofs. in hosted we provide logs and audit trails which customers have used successfully in audits.

[09:05] Priya: what about model weights? if we host fine-tuned models, can we ensure weights don't leave our account?
[09:13] Derek: for Private, yes weights stay in your environment. for Dedicated, model artifacts are stored in customer-dedicated pools (logical isolation) with encryption. hosted stores artifacts in provider buckets; we offer bring-your-own model and encryption to minimize exposure.

[09:40] Sofia: any red flags or must-haves we should know now that would move you to Private instead of hosted?
[09:47] Tom: primary must-have is customer-managed HSM-backed keys plus immutable audit logs in our storage. next is immediate SSO revocation.
[09:56] Marta: and network-level isolation for production traffic.

[10:10] Derek: ok that's helpful. sounds like for prod you'll want Dedicated or Private — pilot can be hosted but with KMS proxy and log export to your bucket to validate controls.

[10:28] Priya: cost vs latency tradeoff — will Dedicated add latency for our inference?
[10:34] Derek: not necessarily — Dedicated gives you dedicated GPU pools so latency typically improves; the larger changes are around cross-region routing. KMS envelope operations have small overhead but we'll bench it.

[10:50] Evan: regarding ISO — you mentioned partial ISO 27001 coverage? can you clarify scope?
[10:57] Sofia: we have ISO 27001 for our core control plane and operations, and we're extending scope for dedicated/private packaging. i'll include scope details in the docs.

[11:14] Tom: auditability question: do logs include full prompt text by default? that is sensitive for us.
[11:21] Derek: by default we redact sensitive fields in logs; prompt capture is configurable — for max privacy we recommend disabling prompt logging and enabling on-demand capture to a customer bucket. we'll show the flags in the deep dive.

[11:40] Priya: can we do on-prem for the entire stack? we have an air-gapped environment for PHI.
[11:47] Derek: Private on-prem package exists; it requires an ops engagement and lead time ~8-12 weeks for install and validation. it supports HSM, local KMS, air-gap. cost and support differ from hosted/dedicated.

[12:05] Sofia: ok let's capture concrete next steps: we'll share SOC2 + subprocessor list, Derek will run scheduling for KMS deep-dive, and we'll propose pilot contract.

[12:16] Marta: can you also share a sample network diagram and peering checklist?
[12:21] Derek: sure — i'll attach the peering checklist and diagram.

[12:30] Tom: are there any known regulatory gaps for healthcare customers?
[12:35] Sofia: we don't certify HIPAA as vendor-level, but we provide controls and BAAs via enterprise package. we'll include BAA template for review.

[12:48] Priya: timeline again — if we start pilot in 2 weeks can we be production-ready by mid-Q2?
[12:55] Derek: yes pilot -> validation -> dedicated/private onboarding fits that cadence; we'll map dependencies in the deep-dive.

[13:10] -- mid call technical dive with Derek --
[13:12] [13:12] Derek: walking through KMS architecture: customer-managed keys via cloud KMS, external key manager using KMIP or KMS proxy, or HSM do we have preference?
[13:27] Marta: prefer HSM-backed keys with HSM policy enforcement; need to see attestations.
[13:35] Derek: we support HSM-backed via customer HSM in Private or by using external KMS with Dedicated. details: we keep only encrypted DEKs on the service, the KEKs live in your KMS.

[14:00] Priya: any change to backup flow? backups must be encrypted with customer keys.
[14:05] Derek: backup encryption uses same key hierarchy; we'll provide backup key handling doc.

[14:22] Tom: do you rotate keys automatically? and can we force rotation?
[14:27] Derek: rotation supported; you can set automatic rotation cadence, or trigger manual rotation via API which will require a brief rewrap operation but we design it to avoid downtime.

[15:00] Priya: logging schema — what fields are included, can we add custom fields?
[15:06] Derek: standard schema includes timestamp, request id, token id (hashed), model id, route, region; we can add custom metadata via request headers and export.

[16:10] -- later section on procurement and legal --
[16:12] Evan: legal will ask for sub-processor list, BAA, SLA, uptime numbers, and incident response playbook. do you provide runbooks?
[16:20] Sofia: yes we provide incident response runbook excerpts and SLA terms in the enterprise package. we'll send a summary and full docs on request.

[17:00] Priya: final clarifying Q: for pilot can you guarantee that logs and model cache remain in our account?
[17:07] Derek: yes for pilot we can set up log export and model artifact storage in your bucket; caching will still route through our runtime but we can configure cache persistence to your storage for validation.

[17:30] Sofia: great, sounds like alignment on next steps. any other questions?
[17:35] Priya: no, thanks. we'll review SOC2 and follow up with legal.
[17:39] Tom: thanks all.
[17:41] Marta: thanks.
[17:45] Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and scheduling.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and filler removed. timestamps approximate. Some product names may be slightly garbled (e.g., "kay-vee cache" for KV cache).

Closing: action items and next steps recorded above.
